answers.how: Fitting the cube's falling positions gives about 539 px/s², so gravity sets the scale to 55 px/m. The cube is about 21 px tall.
The teacup and plate together span about 79 px vertically; dividing by the gravity-derived scale of 55 px/m gives the height.
The plate defines the full width, about 148 px. Dividing by the gravity-derived scale of 55 px/m gives the width.
The fitted falling trajectory has a downward velocity of about 547 px/s at 1.0 s. Dividing by 55 px/m converts it to m/s.
